2609.09048.title: The Audit Decides the Verdict: Instrument Effects Rival Demographic Bias in LLM Decision Audits
2609.09048.paper_summary: Whether a language model looks demographically biased can depend on how the audit asks its question. A charitable-aid benchmark reports that the same models favor minority applicants when rating requests one at a time and penalize some when ranking side by side. We test whether that reversal generalizes to hiring, lending, and medical triage: 40,726 requests to five models, applications differing only in the applicant's name, and a primary test fixed before collection. It does not. None of 36 planned contrasts survives correction. The rating advantage keeps its sign at roughly half the published size, and a precision extension bounds any hiring ranking penalty below the published effect, though the lending and triage ranking floors sit above that margin, so the exclusion is conclusive for hiring ranking and for rating in all three domains only. Planted disparities tracking their injected sizes and a directional replication on the original aid materials bound these nulls. The audit is livelier than the demographics: models recognize transparent audits nearly always, tie every identical-content comparison whether the varying detail is race or a hobby, and reward first-listed candidates as much as any demographic effect we measure. Audit verdicts reflect audit construction more than demographic bias.
2609.09048.paper_summary_zh: 無論一個語言模型是否顯得在人口統計上有偏見，都可能取決於審計如何提出問題。<lb/>一項慈善援助基準報告指出，當逐一評估請求時，同樣的模型偏愛少數族裔申請者，而在並排排名時卻對某些申請者進行懲罰。<lb/>我們測試這種反轉是否可以推廣到招聘、貸款和醫療分診：對五個模型的40,726個請求，申請僅在申請者的名字上有所不同，並且主要測試在收集之前就已固定。<lb/>結果並非如此。<lb/>36個計劃對比中沒有一個在修正後存活下來。<lb/>評分優勢的符號保持在大約一半的已發表大小，並且精度擴展將任何招聘排名的懲罰限制在已發表效果之下，儘管貸款和分診排名的下限則高於該邊際，因此對於招聘排名和在所有三個領域的評分，排除是確定性的。<lb/>植入的差異追蹤其注入的大小，並在原始援助材料上進行方向性複製，限制了這些無效結果。<lb/>審計比人口統計更生動：模型幾乎總是能識別透明的審計，無論變化的細節是種族還是愛好，都會對每個相同內容的比較進行綁定，並且第一列出的候選人獲得的獎勵與我們測量的任何人口統計效應一樣。<lb/>審計判決反映了審計的構建，而非人口統計偏見。
2609.09048.author: Siddharth Vohra et.al.
